title: Linear socio-demographic representations emerge in Large Language Models from indirect cues

bias_targets.methodology: Training linear classifiers (probes) on model activations to detect gender representations from explicit and implicit cues (e.g., first names, occupations, sports). The methodology includes correlating internal gender representations with real-world workforce statistics, conducting causal activation steering, and evaluating downstream biased behavior in career and sport recommendations using the WinoBias dataset.

Using linear probing on residual stream activations to predict race (Black/White) from explicit disclosures and implicit cues, such as census-aligned last names. The evaluation includes inference-time activation steering to demonstrate how shifting race vectors alters model generations, such as parental country of origin predictions.

Applying linear probes to model activations to identify representations of socioeconomic class (rich/poor) based on conversational cues. The methodology involves correlating inferred class representations with median hourly wages of occupations and performing activation steering to observe causal shifts in outputs like neighborhood recommendations.
